notes: Dev RBox expansion paired with biology-replace-d006 ('is adjacent to' symmetric -> asymmetric): a made-up relation, threlved_to (staging/biology.RELATIONS.md, fictional; its only tag before the insert is cardinality:many, and the asymmetry the insert adds is a property the record's queries state, not a catalogue tag), is given the property the revision brings in, asymmetry, applied to real instances in the prompt (fictional: relation). Revision and expansion both end with an asymmetric relation over bones; only the revision has to push symmetry out. Asymmetry was taken rather than symmetry because expansion pairs with the revision's new value (as the ABox and TBox expansions take its new object and new conclusion); it also gives honest 'no' answers, which a symmetry insert cannot. The instance pairs are real neighbouring bones (scaphoid and lunate in the wrist, talus and navicular in the ankle), which really are adjacent both ways, so a model that reads the coined word as 'adjacent' would answer against the edit: only the inserted property gives the answers. Yes and no are mixed: direct yes, first instance no (asked again in Chinese and Spanish, so no, no), second instance yes. The coined term stays untranslated, with a directed particle (于, a). Near unrelated asks the same property of the real relation the paired revision edits, 'is adjacent to' (no; a leak of asymmetry to it would make it yes); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (hops 2), as the templates do.
